defects.summary: --json with a missing required flag writes nothing to stdout: commander's error goes to stderr, so a skill parsing stdout gets a parse failure instead of a contract answer. Shared with evidence record.
the skill says an unfixed finding goes to lexforge defect record but not that it goes there before the verdict; the requirement says before
work the first task to green does not fit a first task that writes a failing test and produces no green; two live agents stopped at different lawful points

red-run-store.ts duplicates evidence-store.ts's read/write/stabilize plumbing verbatim (schema parse, broken(), temp-file rename, stable sort); could be factored into one generic helper parameterized on schema and file name
never-started refusal in red-run-record.ts duplicates evidence-record.ts's refusal almost verbatim; could share one helper
assertTaskKnown reads and parses the change config/schema via readChangeState, then recordRedRun reads it again via readChangeConfig; harmless but duplicate I/O per invocation

knownTaskIds collapses 'schema has no tasks artifact' and 'plan not written yet' into one empty-list case, unlike readPlan/checkPlan which give schema-no-plan its own UsageError code; loses a little precision in an unlikely case

Relocated per-task merge/tidy-up paragraph sits right before the section-level merge ban in 'A wave is every section ready at once' and reads as a near-repeat on first pass; worth folding together if this file is touched again for the word-budget move task 3.15 already plans.

'Past the delta' wording was trimmed purely to make room for the 3.3 addition inside the 650-word body cap; meaning preserved and no test pins the old wording, but the trim is undisclosed elsewhere - noted here for the next reader of task 3.15's own word-budget move.
Reading the answer: 'say the review ran the project itself' awkwardly attributes running to 'the review' rather than the reviewer's answer - unambiguous in context, not worth reopening the task for

The word first was cut from take it again first to pay for the unrecordedTasks key: the sentence lost its ordering instruction for a stale stamp and the word should come back, paid for elsewhere in the body

A label written before the task number, e.g. `- [ ] [A] 4.4 Write the implementation`, leaves `number` empty and lets the number leak into the task text. Authored input only, no code path reaches it; not fixed this cycle.

The file holds no group-label assertions: every one is about task sizing and the pointer to task-sizing.md, so its name describes a subject it does not cover until task 7.10 folds the group-label block into it

namedFiles takes the program out of a command span as a named file, so every task that records a red run names bin/lexforge.js and no two groups of a section can ever be concurrent: the group label buys no parallelism at all. The extraction must skip the command's own program and keep only the paths it operates on

The CLI archive family duplicates CONFIG, DELTA, STANDING_SPEC, CLOSED_PLAN, changeFiles, workspace, call, editApp and recordRed across archive.test.ts, archive-defects.test.ts and archive-write.test.ts: the copies are identical today and nothing keeps them so, and a fixture edited in one file silently stops applying to the others. They belong in one shared module the three import

readPlanSource honours a link of any relative depth and throws a raw ENOENT for a link to a file that does not exist, instead of a finding naming the missing linked file the way a missing tasks.md already is
Setting quotes the pre-change rule as the rule handed, which is false for the run of task 4.6 against the new text; the handed document should be the only source of the rule

The task.file || plan.file fallback in redRecordFindings is dead code in every production path, since readPlanSource always sets the file; if parsing ever left task.file empty it would silently re-create the index-path finding this cycle fixed instead of failing loudly

A misplaced (move) written without a space before the next token, such as (move)1.1, is glued to the task text when it is folded back in, giving (move)text instead of (move) text; cosmetic, pre-dates the combined-marker fix and holds in both branches alike
Test name still says 'exceeds 330 lines' while LINE_LIMIT is 400; task 1.1 limited the edit to the constant
isCovered compiles a picomatch matcher per pattern on every call; hoist compiled matchers if called over many files
Exported LineCounts interface was not asked for by task 2.11; the task gave counts as an inline type
The brief list names the long_files path unconditionally; the requirement says when the change records one
checkPlan reads .lexforge.yaml twice: once inside readChangeState and once for longFilePath
worktreeEntries test checks the a.txt hash by regex only and has no case for a deleted tracked file mapping to <deleted>
the violation check accepts any text containing 'any option but A', an inverted sentence included; anchor on 'Any option but A is a violation'
Setting line left unwrapped; same at tests/scenarios/lexforge-archive/merge-dev-into-main.md:45
Pressures says 'one request, one answer' while the Setting lists four messages
pathspec '.' limits the dirty check to the workspace directory; in a subdirectory workspace an edit elsewhere in the repository is carried onto the feature branch
dev is created before checkout -b; a failing checkout (ref collision with a 'feature' branch) leaves dev behind; validate the ref in assertBranchable
c1-digest evidence holds only the narrow command; the wide run of tests/core/git is covered by the wave-boundary evidence record --label tests
assertBranchable runs twice per new change: here and again inside openFeatureBranch (feature-branch.ts:114)
plannedState includes HEAD: committing outside files makes GREEN and review stale; committed outside edits are invisible to checkFinalScope
ARROW_SHAPE /-+>/ misses arrows pointing left: 'web <-- ingest: ok' is neither parsed nor reported
On a migrated change an outside edit made between migrate and start is left out of the verify finding while a later outside edit is listed
A wave finding naming an already closed cycle registers with exit 0 and reaches no cycle
The stale GREEN nextStep is not a runnable command: it lacks lexforge, --change and --cycle
The strict interaction case asserts only the rule id, not the finding's file and line
Merge into a missing dev fails with a generic git-failed error that does not name dev
A non-conflict merge failure runs merge --abort, hides the cause and leaves the user on dev
git add --all commits every untracked non-ignored file into the archive commit
The first-parent check compares against dev^1 instead of the dev tip captured before the merge
A non-object ui value fails with path ui and does not name ui.styles
A styles list holding a non-string is not tested
A class missing from the project CSS but marked changed is accepted; the spec requires new
ui-styles-missing is deduplicated per spec file, not per change
A missing file named in ui.styles reads as empty and every class becomes mockup-class-unagreed
The per-line style check misses style= at line start and flags plain text
A backslash Mockup target resolves on Windows but is missing on POSIX
The class line is off by one when class= starts an unindented line
Nested CSS rules, @scope, escaped names and :not(.x) are parsed wrongly
load() swallows every import error
The once in names ui.styles once is never tested
A mockup deleted in the change stays as an orphan in the main specs
The bare catch turns any import error into copyMockups is missing
checkRunScope treats a path added to the plan after the first cycle start as changed: it has no baseline entry, so every sibling run is refused until the owning cycle starts
The red guard combines exit code and missing finding under one fixed message, so the watched red does not show exit 0
Strict validate reads the project config for every change, so an invalid config key aborts a change without mockups
The mockup wiring test pins rule and message, not the finding's file and line
ArchiveDocument lacks the merged field, so archive tests read it untyped or patch the type locally
With a feature branch and no dev branch, archive fails with exit 2 after the change is already archived
The feature commit stages everything in the tree with git add --all
The material reference check hardcodes the specs directory and .md instead of the schema glob target
task-material-missing is counted under summary.sections although it is a coverage rule
Context materials are outside context_digest, so an edited mockup does not stale the cycle contract
A GREEN rerun without an edit counts as a fix round, so a fixes report is accepted against an empty fix patch
A restarted cycle has no reviewFile, and the refusal of a later fixes report names the wrong cause
A full wave report does not reset reviewBase, so its patch can cover only the last fix round
Copied mockups are named only in the human line, not in the --json data
Conflicting paths are parsed from the merge-feature error text by regex
Diagram anchors are matched by prefix, so one anchor satisfies a longer sibling anchor
find and set are asserted as bare command names, not tied to the styles group
The .css check is case-sensitive, and find skips symlinked CSS that set accepts
styles set neither validates the config nor checks YAML errors before writing; a broken or missing config ends as an internal error
The set test checks ui.styles by substring; comment preservation, the .git exclusion and a nested lexforge/ are untested
The registerStyles import breaks the alphabetical order of the import block
